hey all. i remember someone once mentioned a way to test specific aspects of your bots so u didnt have to roleplay up to it. anyone know what im talking about?

Yes it was me! So when I do testing I do a few things. First, I usually drop the personality in with a shell scenario and opening line and test the personality to see if it gives me the character responses I want. I'll push it's buttons and see if it reacts the way I want. If it doesn't, I play with the personality traits until it works the way I want.

Then I start to build in my scenario and refine. But I also use out of character commands to interrogate responses I don't expect. I'll ask it why is it generating a certain response or believes a certain thing... and sometimes I can get insight into why the AI is making certain choices.

(I once tried to have sex with a character I was testing and she refused. The out of character commands revealed that my instruction of "The character will have a night of passion with the user" was interpreted as having a night of passionate talk about poetry and art, not sex).
Is that what you were looking for?

does anyone know how i can add body measurements for my bot?

truth is those measurements are probably never going to be used in a chat response. if theres a fetish youre aiming for, for the height/weight put it as "much lighter/heavier than {{user}}" so that it becomes relative, and during sex it tries to keep in mind that fact.
the problem is numeric measurements get lost and wastes tokens. so instead of saying "large breasts", you can say something like "the bot's breasts large enough to smother {{user}}'s head"

if u really want to emphasize the body attributes... can even do an instruction block in your scenario. sex positions: [ doggy style: [ {{char}}'s ass ripples on impact ] missionary: [ {{char}}'s breasts engulfs {{user}}'s head ] ]
these kinds of instructions really tell the bot how to write its responses way better than numeric measurements
facial expression is CRITICAL. a lot of people wont want to hear this but the image is the most important factor in determining the success of your character bot.
it does not matter how well-written your character is if the image doesnt give sweaty neckbeards a boner. thats just how it is i dont make the rules.

avoid bland facial expressions. depending on the scenario my favorite keywords for facial expression are "surprised expression", "frustrated expression", "frustrated and surprised expression", and "angry expression"
im trying to tweak a bot thats basically a succubus whos forced to obey any order given, but does so with malicious compliance.

i want her to actively be trying to kill you while being completely bound to obey your orders, but if you like tell her to get you a drink she could just get you a poisoned drink... but the bot wont commit to actual lethal intent.
im pretty sure ive seen other bots where you can die pretty easily so its possible to make a bot thats out to get you right?
it most certainly is! just dont go too crazy with the murderous personality traits or itll get flagged against guidelines

i used to waste my tokens on so much useless stuff. try something like this. [Instruction(When {{char}} delivers the food to {{user}}, if user did not request no poisoning, {{char}} will poison the food. Poisoned food will cause the {{user}} to die by asphyxiation)].
you could attempt a more broad one and test it too. to see if the LLM will pick up on your intent. realistically youll never 100% know what the bot will do

in my experience you can create a bot thats successful in popularity that has very few tokens used in creation. if you have a very simple premise, "Woman stuck in a wall" for example, how many tokens do you really need to invest in that? slap a sexy image on it and im sure you will get plays with barely any personality or scenario.

but if you arent interested in just creating popular bots, but complex bots that create moments, well it takes tokens. so the question comes down to why you want to create a bot that uses only 1K tokens.
from an artistic standpoint i often find creative growth using constraints. it would be an interesting challenge to create a bot that was restricted to only 1K tokens and see what you could build

How do i make the bot not write an entire essay in response? I want it to take one action at a time. Not play out an entire scene without giving me chance to react or do anything.
Simply reduce the Response tokens in the settings and enable Trim incomplete responses. This regulates the maximum number of tokens that the API will generate to respond.
